research_analysis.exact_observed_hook: No speech. On-screen text: "Nashville airport baggage claim was designed by elite engineers"
research_analysis.visual_hook: Wide static shot of baggage carousel 12 with two suitcases already lying on the floor beside the moving belt.
research_analysis.narrative_structure: One static 8-second shot with one sarcastic caption. The footage supplies the punchline on its own: around 0:05 another suitcase falls off the belt, and at 0:07 a passenger walks up to collect his bag from the floor.
research_analysis.viral_mechanism: Sarcastic praise over real footage of something obviously badly designed. The creator adds nothing but the caption, and the viewer does the work of noticing.
research_analysis.observed_evidence: 3.9M views, 263.5x the creator's 14.8K median, 5.7K followers. 0 cuts, no speech, comedic pizzicato music plus the thud of a bag falling. Loops. No CTA. The caption tags the specific airport.
research_analysis.performance_hypothesis: Hypothesis: naming a specific place pulls in everyone who has been there to confirm it in the comments, and locals share it. The loop lets viewers wait for the bag to fall a second time.
research_analysis.why_this_format_fits_alex: His biggest Reel is a place joke about a parking lot (Central Park, 13.5M). He now lives in a state famous for enormous parking lots, so he can make the real-footage version of his own hit with no editing.
research_analysis.originality_changes: Borrowed: static real-world shot plus one line of sarcastic praise naming a place. New: the place is Florida, the subject is a vast empty parking lot with his car alone in it and him as a tiny figure walking across, and it links back to his own Central Park joke.

alex_adaptation.concept: A locked-off wide shot of an absurdly large, nearly empty Florida parking lot. One small car far away. A tiny Alex walks the whole distance toward a store on the horizon. The caption praises the planners.
alex_adaptation.target_audience: Floridians, anyone who has visited Florida, and the audience that shared the Central Park Reel.
alex_adaptation.first_frame: Extreme wide shot of a huge sun-bleached parking lot, hundreds of empty spaces, one Lexus parked alone in the middle distance, a store entrance tiny at the top of the frame. Text is on screen.

full_script.speaker: None
full_script.action: Alex, very small in frame, gets out of the Lexus, shuts the door, and starts walking toward the distant store. Normal pace. He does not acknowledge the camera.
full_script.camera: Phone on a tall tripod or resting on a car roof at the far edge of the lot, widest lens, locked off.
full_script.on_screen_text: "Florida was designed by someone who really loved parking"
full_script.editing: No cuts. Text on for the full 9 seconds, top third, over sky.
full_script.audio: Light, slightly silly instrumental from the Instagram library. Distant traffic.

full_script.speaker: None
full_script.action: He keeps walking. He is not noticeably closer to the store. Around 6 seconds he stops, puts his hands on his hips, looks at how far is left, looks back at the car, and resumes walking with his shoulders dropped.
full_script.editing: End while he is still mid-lot so the loop restarts with him at the car.
full_script.audio: Music continues. A single seagull cry at 6s when he stops.

alternate_hooks: "Florida saw my Central Park video and took notes"
"Moved to Florida. Found where they put Central Park."
alternate_endings: At 6 seconds he gives up, turns around, walks back to the car and drives the remaining distance to a closer space.
Hold the wide shot with no person in it at all for the last 3 seconds, just heat shimmer, then a second line: "I'm in this photo. Good luck."
alex_adaptation.caption: I made a joke about paving Central Park. Florida didn't know it was a joke.

production.location: The largest, emptiest parking lot he can find: a mall, stadium or big-box store at an off hour. Film from the far edge.
props: Tall tripod or a stable high surface
production.wardrobe: Something with contrast against asphalt so the tiny figure reads: white tee, dark shorts.
shot_list: One locked-off extreme wide, record 60 seconds: exit car, walk, stop at the midpoint with hands on hips, continue. Do 2 takes.
production.editor_instructions: Pick the 9 seconds where he exits the car and reaches the hands-on-hips stop. No zoom: the smallness is the joke. Text over the sky. Do not show store signage or other people's license plates legibly.

variants_to_test: Alternate hook: "Florida saw my Central Park video and took notes"
Alternate payoff: He gives up and drives to a closer space
testing.promotion_decision: Brand fit 2 (3 if the Central Park callback hook is used). Promote if 48h views reach 3x the trailing median and shares per 1,000 reached are top quartile; treat as a reach play and judge the series on whether profile visits rise.
follow_up_variations_if_successful: Static shot of a sidewalk that ends in grass: "Florida's walking infrastructure is world class"
Static shot of a six-lane road with one crosswalk in the distance: "Florida wants you to drive to the mailbox"
Static shot of three identical strip malls in a row: "Florida has incredible variety"

creative_confidence.rationale: A real-footage sequel to his biggest hit, in the same silent one-shot form, and it takes twenty minutes. On its own it could sit on a meme page, so the caption and the callback hook are doing the identity work.
uncertainties: The picture is less surprising than a doctored Central Park; reach could be far lower.
The callback hook only works for people who saw the first Reel.
He needs to find a lot that is visibly huge and visibly empty.
